title: Line-graph colourings and matching decompositions
abstract: Connects Mathlib line-graph colourings to palette-indexed partitions of actual graph edges into Mathlib matching subgraphs. Both conversions are inverse, preserve each matching exactly, and allow empty colours without a default colour or a finiteness assumption. An edge equivalence yields exact edge accounting: natural-number counts require only finite edges and a finite palette, while indexed cardinal counts allow arbitrary vertices, edges, and palettes. This is classical representation interoperability, not a new colouring bound or a claim of priority.

informal.SimpleGraph.lineGraphColoringEquivMatchi: Proper colourings of the line graph on any palette are equivalent to partitions of the original edges into matching subgraphs indexed by that palette, with empty classes permitted.
informal.SimpleGraph.MatchingDecomposition.edgeMa: Converting a matching decomposition to a colouring and extracting one colour class returns exactly its original matching subgraph.
informal.SimpleGraph.MatchingDecomposition.edgeEq: Original graph edges are in bijection with the disjoint union of the edge types of the palette-indexed matching subgraphs.
informal.SimpleGraph.MatchingDecomposition.card_e: For a finite edge set and finite palette, the number of graph edges equals the sum of the numbers of edges in its matching classes, even when the vertex set is infinite.
informal.SimpleGraph.MatchingDecomposition.cardin: Without any finiteness assumption on vertices, edges, or colours, the cardinality of the graph edge set equals the indexed cardinal sum of the matching-class edge cardinalities, with a universe lift on the graph edge cardinality when required.
informal.SimpleGraph.lineGraph_colorable_iff_matc: The line graph is k-colourable if and only if the graph edges decompose into k matchings, allowing unused colours.
